blocks.x: OEE +7.2 points across 14 plants — sensor fabric to scheduling decisions
A global automotive OEM — Manufacturing & Industrial engagement delivered by a 31-person team over 20 months, Global scope, commercial model: build-transfer.

items: Legacy lines uninstrumented; OEE components estimated; changeover losses structurally accepted.
Quality escapes discovered at customer complaints; inspection by sampling.
Flat plant networks left lines exposed to ransomware.

blocks.x: We retrofitted sensor network on live lines (OPC UA/Sparkplug with data contracts), deployed vision inspection closing loops into andon/MES, and gave planners a Swarm scheduling assistant proposing changeover-aware sequences. IEC 62443 zoning preceded instrumentation — security first, then telemetry, then decisions on Forge.
A global automotive OEM uses the standard Achala delivery pattern — nothing bespoke about the governance, everything bespoke about the design. That split is deliberate.

items: The committed move on this metric: 10x, measured against the baseline signed in week two
A global gaming studio (live-service title, 15M MAU)
The measured delta and the method note are written up on the case page — anonymized by agreement, baseline audited.

blocks.x: Towers: IoT, Digital Twin & Robotics, Agentic AI & Hyperautomation, Data, Analytics & Lakehouse, Cybersecurity & Zero-Trust. Platforms: BI & Analytics Platform, KYC Management System, Fleet Management System.

items: What moved unchanged between sectors, and why it was safe to move — stated plainly.
What does not transfer between estates, and the adaptation it needs — named before the pilot, not after.

blocks.x: Anonymity is contractual; the measurement discipline is not — the same gates and evidence standards apply on every engagement.
The diagnostic that locked this baseline is a two-week exercise; the briefing explains what it would find in your estate.
